A1.justification: Both 20-page PDFs describe DSH-Bench, with readable and matchable text, equations, tables, and figures. Neither contains appendices: both end with references despite citing supplementary Sections B, D, and E. The comparison therefore covers all supplied material, but not those unavailable supplements.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of 19 generation models, human-alignment measurements for SICS, and analyses across subject categories, difficulty levels, and prompt scenarios.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds an original analysis relating difficulty labels to objective image-complexity measures in Table 1.

M1.justification: The taxonomy construction, difficulty-labeling procedure, prompt generation, and Qwen2.5-VL-7B-based SICS remain unchanged. The new complexity analysis validates existing labels rather than changing their assignment or the generation/evaluation method.

E1.justification: Reported coverage remains 459 subjects, 58 categories, three difficulty levels, and six scenarios comprising 5,508 prompts, with the same comparison benchmarks. The new validation samples existing images. Removing Pinterest from the sourcing description does not establish a change in represented subjects, domains, or tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in v2 Tables 1–3 and corresponding v3 Tables 2–4, including the 19-model leaderboard. Newly cited RefVNLI and MMIG-Bench are discussed as related work, not evaluated as additional comparators.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 adds a validation protocol sampling 50 images per difficulty level and measuring Canny edge density, GLCM contrast, and JPEG bits/pixel at quality factor 85. Existing generation-evaluation settings remain unchanged. The newly stated 1,600-pair held-out set documents an existing experiment rather than establishing a revised split.

E4.justification: v3 adds a focused validation of whether difficulty labels track model-independent image complexity, reporting increasing complexity across tiers in Table 1. The existing category, difficulty, scenario, and qualitative analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The new difficulty-validation study reports five independent sampling runs, mean ± standard deviation, and p-values for Spearman correlations. v2 contains no corresponding uncertainty or significance reporting for this analysis. These additions do not establish increased repetition of the retained benchmark experiments.

E6.justification: New Table 1 reports positive difficulty correlations of 0.367, 0.235, and 0.260 for edge density, GLCM contrast, and JPEG bits/pixel, respectively, all with p < 0.01. All scores in the three matched original tables remain identical, as do Figure 8's plotted results. The introductory category-expansion figure changes from 8× to 9×.

T1.justification: The difficulty definitions and weighted harmonic aggregation in Equation 1 are retained. The added complexity validation is empirical; it introduces no new mathematical definition, theorem, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: The Introduction corrects the category-expansion claim from 8× to 9× and the takeaway summary from fifteen evaluated methods to 19. The underlying category counts and 19-model evaluation were already present in v2. The principal contributions and SICS alignment claim are otherwise unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new complexity correlations as evidence that difficulty labels reflect intrinsic image properties rather than circular model-dependent criteria. It also explicitly argues that the disjoint SICS evaluation set supports genuine human alignment rather than training-data fitting. Existing performance interpretations and applicability boundaries remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies that the SICS human-alignment evaluation uses 1,600 pairs disjoint from its 5,000 training pairs. It supplies a repository address and changes the conclusion from promised to stated public availability. Section 3.1 removes Pinterest from documented image provenance without explaining whether any images were replaced.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds brief discussions and references for RefVNLI's joint evaluation and MMIG-Bench's broader multimodal coverage. This modestly updates related-work coverage without substantially changing DSH-Bench's positioning.

P1.justification: v3 replaces the affiliation placeholder with Tencent and contact information, adds short validation and held-out-set explanations, and corrects counts and figure references. The abstract, section order, and most narrative wording remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the difficulty-validation table, relocates Figure 1 after the abstract, and reflows existing figures and tables. Figure 4 removes Pinterest from its collection diagram. Existing result displays retain their content; there is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 provides additional empirical support for the difficulty tiers, clarifies separation of SICS training and evaluation data, and supplies concrete access information. These improve evidential support and reproducibility documentation while leaving the principal results unchanged. The unexplained sourcing revision limits provenance clarity, but the supported gains still indicate a modest overall improvement.
